step1_analysis.description: This circuit is a small-signal macro-model of an active-feedback frequency-compensated (AFFC) multistage amplifier. It models the output impedances, load capacitance, and the compensation network (Ca, ra) used to introduce a zero for phase margin improvement.

paper_reference.title: Active-Feedback Frequency-Compensation Technique for Low-Power Multistage Amplifiers

dc_gain.description: Low-frequency transimpedance gain of the output node

sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on typical output resistance values in small-signal models to match the 100 dB gain reported in the paper.
Calculated from the RC time constant of the output node using the 100 pF load capacitance reported in the paper.
The provided netlist contains only passive components and ideal AC current sources, so DC power from a voltage supply is zero.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure transimpedance gain and bandwidth of the small-signal model.
step3_testbench.spice:
* AFFC Small-Signal Model Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param R1_val=100k
.param C1_val=11p
.param ra_val=1k
.param Ca_val=3p
.param RL_val=100k
.param CL_val=100p

* DUT
R1 V2 GND {R1_val}
C1 V2 GND {C1_val}
I1 GND V2 DC 0 AC 1
ra Va GND {ra_val}
Ca Va Vo {Ca_val}
I2 Vo GND DC 0 AC 1
RL Vo GND {RL_val}
CL Vo GND {CL_val}

* Dummy VDD for power measurement
Vdd VDD GND 1.8

.control
op
let power = -i(Vdd)*1.8
print power

ac dec 100 1 100Meg
let gain_db = vdb(Vo)
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=1
meas ac bw when gain_db='dc_gain-3' fall=1
quit
.endc
.end
